AR|Arkadelphia.intro: Arkadelphia is a college town of about 10,400 people and the county seat of Clark County. It sits at the foothills of the Ouachita Mountains on Interstate 30 between Little Rock and Texarkana.
family: Henderson State University and Ouachita Baptist University are both in the city.
The Arkadelphia Arts Center hosts exhibits, productions and educational workshops.
The Reynolds Science Center Planetarium is on the Henderson State campus.
outdoors: DeGray Lake, on the Caddo River, has 208 miles of shoreline and 13,800 acres of water.
DeGray Lake Resort State Park offers fishing, swimming, boating, hiking, horseback riding and an 18-hole golf course.
Hot Springs National Park, under an hour away, has hiking trails and camping areas.
sports: Henderson State's Reddies compete in NCAA Division II in the Great American Conference.
Henderson State and Ouachita Baptist share the longest rivalry in Division II football, the Battle of the Ravine, which began in 1895.
AR|Arkadelphia.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Arkadelphia far below the US average, with groceries, utilities and other everyday costs somewhat below it.
AR|Arkadelphia.climate: Summers are hot and humid and winters are generally mild to cool. Typical daily highs are about 55°F in January and about 94°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Hot Springs, under an hour away.
The main VA medical center for central Arkansas is in Little Rock, about an hour and 15 minutes away.
around: Interstate 30 runs through town.
Hot Springs is under an hour away by car and Little Rock about an hour and 15 minutes.
Texarkana is about an hour and a half away.

AL|Semmes.intro: Semmes is a small city of about 5,000 people in western Mobile County, part of the Mobile metropolitan area. It became a city in 2011.
family: Semmes School, a restored 1902 one-room school, is listed as an Alabama historical landmark.
The battleship USS Alabama, commissioned in 1942, is a museum ship docked in Mobile.
Mobile is known for Mardi Gras, the oldest organized Carnival celebration in the United States.
outdoors: Dauphin Island, a barrier island town in Mobile County, has beaches, popular fishing waters and the Dauphin Island Sea Lab.
Gulf State Park covers a large part of Gulf Shores, a Gulf of Mexico resort city about an hour and 45 minutes away.
sports: The University of South Alabama Jaguars play in the Sun Belt Conference and field 17 varsity sports.
The Senior Bowl, a college football all-star game, is played in Mobile each year in late January or early February.
AL|Semmes.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Semmes well below the US average, with groceries and utilities close to average.
AL|Semmes.climate: Semmes has a subtropical climate with mild, wet winters and very hot, humid summers, and the area can see hurricanes. Typical highs are about 60°F in January and about 91°F in July and August.
around: Downtown Mobile is about half an hour away by car.
U.S. Route 98, also called Moffett Road, is the main highway through Semmes and leads southeast into Mobile.

AL|Evergreen.intro: Evergreen is a small city of about 3,500 people and the county seat of Conecuh County in south Alabama. Interstate 65 passes the edge of town, about 75 miles from Montgomery and 90 miles from Mobile.
family: The town holds an annual Collard Green Festival, a nod to its 1973 designation as the collard green capital of Alabama.
Monroeville, about 45 minutes away, is known as the Literary Capital of Alabama and is the hometown of Harper Lee.
The battleship USS Alabama is a museum ship in Mobile, a little under two hours away.
outdoors: Conecuh National Forest covers about 83,000 acres in neighboring Covington and Escambia counties.
Open Pond Recreation Area in the forest offers hiking, fishing, bicycling and camping around a sinkhole lake.
The 20-mile Conecuh Trail runs through longleaf pine stands and hardwood bottomlands.
sports: The Montgomery Biscuits play Double-A baseball in Montgomery, about an hour and 40 minutes away.
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos play Double-A baseball in Pensacola, Florida, about two hours away.
AL|Evergreen.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Evergreen well below the US average, with groceries slightly below and utilities slightly above.
AL|Evergreen.climate: Summers are hot, with typical daily highs of about 91°F in July. Winters are mild, with typical highs of about 59°F in January.
vets: The VA lists a clinic in Monroeville, about 45 minutes away.
The main VA location for central Alabama is in Montgomery, about an hour and 40 minutes away.
around: Interstate 65 runs northeast to Montgomery and southwest to Mobile.
Montgomery is about an hour and 40 minutes away by car and Mobile a little under two hours.
Pensacola, Florida, is about two hours away.

AZ|Goodyear.intro: Goodyear is a suburb west of Phoenix in Maricopa County, with about 118,000 residents. It began as cotton farmland bought by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company.
family: The city hall complex includes a public library and a two-acre park.
The White Tank Library and Nature Center offers nature programs for children, families and adults.
Franklin Pierce University has had a campus in Goodyear since 2008.
outdoors: Estrella Mountain Regional Park covers almost 20,000 acres of mostly desert, with more than 30 miles of trails.
White Tank Mountain Regional Park covers nearly 29,300 acres of desert and mountain, with almost 26 miles of hiking trails.
The Gila River passes through the city.
sports: Goodyear Ballpark hosts spring training for the Cleveland Guardians and Cincinnati Reds.
Phoenix Raceway in neighboring Avondale hosts two NASCAR race weekends a year.
AZ|Goodyear.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Goodyear well above the US average, with groceries, utilities and other everyday costs close to average.
AZ|Goodyear.climate: Goodyear has a hot desert climate with more than 300 sunny days a year. Winters are mild, with typical highs around 65°F in January, and summers are very hot, with July highs averaging about 105°F.
vets: The Phoenix VA medical center is in Phoenix, about half an hour away.
The VA also lists clinics in Surprise and in southwest Phoenix.
Luke Air Force Base is in the Glendale area, about half an hour away.
around: Phoenix is about half an hour away by car.
Glendale is also about half an hour away.
Tucson is about two and a half hours away.

AZ|Parker.intro: Parker is a town of about 3,400 people on the Colorado River and the county seat of La Paz County. It is also the headquarters of the Colorado River Indian Tribes.
family: The Colorado River Indian Tribes museum in Parker displays historical and contemporary artwork, especially ceramics, made by tribal citizens.
The Old Parker Jail, built in 1914, stands in a city park and is on the National Register of Historic Places.
Lake Havasu City, about 45 minutes away, is home to London Bridge.
outdoors: Buckskin Mountain State Park, near Parker, has Colorado River shoreline, camping and water recreation.
Parker Dam on the Colorado River creates Lake Havasu.
Blythe, California, a little over an hour away, has parks and boat ramps onto the Colorado River.
AZ|Parker.cost: BestPlaces index figures put groceries and housing in Parker a little below the US average, with utilities slightly above.
AZ|Parker.climate: Parker has an arid climate with very little rain, warm winters and extremely hot summers. Typical daily highs run from about 69°F in January to about 108°F in July.
vets: The VA lists a clinic in Lake Havasu City, about 45 minutes away.
Another VA clinic is in Kingman, about two hours away.
around: Lake Havasu City is about 45 minutes away by car.
Quartzsite, about 40 minutes away, hosts major gem and mineral shows, mostly in January and February.
Phoenix is about three hours away.

AZ|Prescott.intro: Prescott is a city of about 46,000 people and the county seat of Yavapai County, known for its historic downtown and Whiskey Row. It was once the capital of the Arizona Territory and is home to several colleges, including Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University's Prescott campus.
family: The Sharlot Hall Museum houses much of Prescott's territorial history.
The Heritage Park Zoo is in Prescott.
The courthouse plaza, a lawn under large old elm trees, hosts cultural events and performances on many summer nights.
outdoors: The Granite Dells, just north of the city center, are granite boulder formations with hiking trails that connect to the Peavine Trail.
Lynx Lake, set among tall ponderosa pines, offers boating, camping, fishing, hiking and mountain biking.
Goldwater Lake is a popular park with picnic facilities.
sports: Frontier Days, which bills itself as the World's Oldest Rodeo, has run every year since 1888 in the days leading up to July 4.
Four golf courses lie within the city limits, and two of them are city courses.
AZ|Prescott.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Prescott far above the US average, with groceries and utilities close to average.
AZ|Prescott.climate: Typical daily highs are about 53°F in January and about 90°F in July. A summer monsoon season brings rain and thunderstorms, and winter snowfall is typically light.
vets: The Northern Arizona VA Health Care System has its main medical center in Prescott.
VA outpatient clinics are also in Cottonwood, Flagstaff and other northern Arizona communities.
around: Prescott Regional Airport, about 7 miles north of the courthouse, has commercial service.
State Route 89A connects Prescott with Cottonwood and Sedona.
State Route 69 leads east to neighboring Prescott Valley.

AZ|Florence.intro: Florence is a town of about 27,000 people and the county seat of Pinal County. It sits on the south bank of the Gila River in the Sonoran Desert, between Phoenix and Tucson.
family: The historic downtown is a National Historic District with over 25 buildings on the National Register of Historic Places.
McFarland State Historic Park holds the first Pinal County Courthouse, built in 1876.
Casa Grande Ruins National Monument in nearby Coolidge preserves Hohokam structures from about 1150 to 1450.
outdoors: Picacho Peak State Park, between Casa Grande and Tucson, is known for spring wildflowers and steep trails with cables and catwalks.
The Superstition Mountains, east of the Phoenix area, have many hiking trails and include Lost Dutchman State Park.
Boyce Thompson Arboretum, near Superior, has more than 2,600 species of arid land plants and a 1.5-mile loop trail.
sports: The Florence Jr. Parada is described as the oldest junior rodeo in the United States.
The Phoenix Suns play in the NBA and the Arizona Diamondbacks in Major League Baseball, both in Phoenix.
Central Arizona College, near Coolidge, fields junior college teams in NJCAA Division I.
AZ|Florence.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Florence about even with the US average, with groceries a little lower and utilities slightly higher.
AZ|Florence.climate: Florence has a hot desert climate with mild winters and hot summers. Typical daily highs are about 66°F in January and about 102°F in July, and much of the summer rain comes with the monsoon from July through September.
vets: The VA lists clinics in Casa Grande.
The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for southern Arizona.
around: Phoenix and Tucson are each roughly an hour to an hour and a half away by car.
Casa Grande and Mesa are each about an hour away.

AZ|Payson.intro: Payson is a mountain town of about 16,000 people in northern Gila County, at about 5,000 feet of elevation. It sits within the Tonto National Forest below the Mogollon Rim.
family: Green Valley Park and Rumsey Park are the town's main parks, and there is a small skate park.
Green Valley Park has a replica of the cabin of author Zane Grey, who wrote about the area.
The August Doin's Rodeo has been held every year since 1884 and is called the world's oldest continuous rodeo.
outdoors: The town is surrounded by the Tonto National Forest.
Tonto Natural Bridge State Park, just northwest of Payson, holds what is described as the largest known natural bridge in the world.
Cold water lakes on top of the Mogollon Rim, north of Payson, are stocked with fish.
sports: The Phoenix Suns play in the NBA and the Arizona Diamondbacks in Major League Baseball, both in Phoenix.
AZ|Payson.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Payson somewhat above the US average, with groceries slightly below.
AZ|Payson.climate: Winters are mild with cold nights, with typical daily highs of about 56°F in January. Summer highs reach about 93°F in July, and monsoon thunderstorms from July through September bring a large share of the year's rain.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Payson, part of the Phoenix VA system.
The same system has clinics in Show Low and Globe, and its main medical center is in Phoenix.
around: State Route 87, the Beeline Highway, leads to the Phoenix area, roughly an hour and a half to two hours away by car.
State Route 260 leads east to Show Low, roughly two hours away.

AZ|Phoenix.intro: Phoenix is the capital of Arizona and its largest city, with about 1.6 million residents. It sits in the Salt River Valley in the Sonoran Desert.
family: The Phoenix Zoo in the Papago Park area has a children's trail with a petting zoo.
ZooLights, a December lighting show at the zoo, has run every year since 1991.
The Heard Museum, founded in 1929, is dedicated to American Indian art.
outdoors: South Mountain Park and Preserve has 58 miles of trails for hiking, cycling and horseback riding.
Camelback Mountain, North Mountain and Piestewa Peak rise within the heart of the valley.
The Desert Botanical Garden in Papago Park has more than 50,000 plants.
sports: The Arizona Diamondbacks, Phoenix Suns, Arizona Cardinals and Phoenix Mercury play in MLB, the NBA, the NFL and the WNBA.
The Phoenix area hosts the 15 major league teams of the Cactus League for spring training.
AZ|Phoenix.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Phoenix well above the US average, with groceries slightly below average and utilities close to it.
AZ|Phoenix.climate: Summers are long and extremely hot and winters are short and mild, with typical daily highs from about 68°F in January to about 107°F in July. Rain is scarce, and a summer monsoon season brings humidity and heavy, localized storms.
vets: The Phoenix VA medical center is in the city, with VA clinics in Mesa, Scottsdale, Gilbert, Surprise and other valley cities.
An Arizona Air National Guard air refueling wing is based at Phoenix Sky Harbor.
around: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, Arizona's largest and busiest, is about 3 miles east of downtown.
Tucson is roughly two hours away by car.
Flagstaff is roughly two and a half hours away.

AZ|Fort Mohave.intro: Fort Mohave is a community of about 16,000 people in western Mohave County, along the Colorado River just south of Bullhead City.
family: The Colorado River Museum in Bullhead City has replicas of area landmarks, Native American artifacts and historical displays.
Fort Mohave has a Mohave County Library branch.
Rotary Park in Bullhead City covers 300 acres of riverfront with beaches, a fishing jetty and boat launch ramps.
outdoors: Lake Mohave, a Colorado River reservoir near Bullhead City, is popular for swimming, kayaking, fishing, boating and water skiing.
Havasu National Wildlife Refuge protects 30 river miles of the lower Colorado River between Needles, California, and Lake Havasu City.
sports: Bullhead City hosts a youth soccer tournament at Rotary Park every February.
Bullhead City also sponsors senior softball tournaments each spring and fall.
AZ|Fort Mohave.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Fort Mohave below the US average, with groceries and utilities a little below it.
AZ|Fort Mohave.climate: The area has a desert climate with mild winters and very hot summers. In neighboring Bullhead City, typical highs are about 65°F in January and about 111°F in July.
vets: The VA lists clinics in Kingman and in Lake Havasu City.
around: Needles, California, is about half an hour away by car.
Lake Havasu City, home to London Bridge, is roughly an hour and 20 minutes away.
Las Vegas and its international airport are a little over two hours away.

AZ|Show Low.intro: Show Low is a city of about 12,000 people in Navajo County, on the Mogollon Rim in east central Arizona.
family: Northland Pioneer College has its White Mountain Campus in Show Low.
A city-run bus links Show Low with Pinetop-Lakeside, Taylor, Snowflake and Holbrook.
outdoors: The city is surrounded by extensive forests and is a popular recreation area.
The Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests cover about 2.76 million acres along the Mogollon Rim and the White Mountains.
Petrified Forest National Park is 28 miles east of Holbrook, which is roughly an hour from Show Low.
AZ|Show Low.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Show Low above the US average, with groceries below it.
AZ|Show Low.climate: Winters are cold, with typical daily highs around 46°F in January, and summers are warm, with highs around 85°F in July. Rain peaks in summer with the monsoon.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Show Low, part of the Phoenix VA system.
The system's main medical center is in Phoenix.
around: Pinetop-Lakeside is the neighboring town, roughly 20 minutes away by car.
Holbrook is roughly an hour away and Payson roughly two hours.
Phoenix is roughly three and a half hours away.

AZ|Yuma.intro: Yuma is a city of about 96,000 people on the Colorado River in the southwest corner of Arizona. It is the county seat of Yuma County.
family: Yuma Territorial Prison, which operated from 1876 to 1909, is now a historic park and museum.
Colorado River State Historic Park, on the site of a former army supply depot, has exhibits on the river and its steamboat era.
outdoors: The Colorado River runs along the north and west sides of town.
The Kofa mountain range and wildlife refuge are nearby, along with Martinez and Mittry lakes.
The Algodones Dunes, a few miles west of Yuma, are a large dune field where off-road riding is allowed in parts.
food: Yuma County supplies a large share of the nation's leafy vegetables from November to March, and the city is known as the Winter Lettuce Capital of the World.
The area grows more than 175 types of crops.
sports: The Yuma Jaycees Silver Spur Rodeo is held every February and opens with a parade.
AZ|Yuma.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Yuma well below the US average, with groceries slightly below and utilities slightly above.
AZ|Yuma.climate: Yuma has a hot desert climate with mild, dry winters and extremely hot summers. Typical highs are about 70°F in January and about 108°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Yuma, and the main VA medical center for southern Arizona is in Tucson.
Yuma is home to Marine Corps Air Station Yuma, and the Army's Yuma Proving Ground is in the area.
around: Yuma International Airport is the city's airport, and Interstate 8 runs west to San Diego.
El Centro, California, is roughly an hour away by car.
San Diego and Phoenix are each roughly three hours away.

AZ|Rio Rico.intro: Rio Rico is a community of more than 20,000 people in Santa Cruz County, just north of Nogales in southern Arizona.
family: Tumacácori National Historical Park protects the ruins of three Spanish mission communities and a 1937 museum building.
Tubac, an artists' colony on the Santa Cruz River, is roughly 25 minutes away.
Reid Park, Tucson's largest park, includes the Reid Park Zoo.
outdoors: Rio Rico sits where Sonoita Creek meets the Santa Cruz River.
Patagonia Lake State Park is a few miles from the town of Patagonia, which is roughly 45 minutes away.
food: Tucson was the first American city named a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, in 2015.
The Sonoita-Elgin wine country is about 20 miles east of Nogales.
AZ|Rio Rico.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and groceries in Rio Rico below the US average, with utilities slightly above.
AZ|Rio Rico.climate: In neighboring Nogales, typical daily highs run from about 66°F in January to about 97°F in June. The summer monsoon generally runs through July and August and brings much of the year's rain.
vets: The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for southern Arizona.
VA clinics are also listed in Green Valley and Sierra Vista.
around: Nogales, the county seat, is roughly 20 minutes away by car.
Tucson, the largest city in southern Arizona, is a little over an hour away.

AZ|Williams.intro: Williams is a small city of about 3,200 people in Coconino County, known as the Gateway to the Grand Canyon. It sits on Historic Route 66 and Interstate 40, about 42 miles west of Flagstaff.
family: The historic downtown covers six blocks, and Williams was the last town on Route 66 to be bypassed by Interstate 40.
Buckskinner Park has basketball and volleyball courts and a regularly stocked fishing lake.
Cataract Lake County Park has a stocked lake, barbecue areas and a playground.
outdoors: Bill Williams Mountain rises to 9,256 feet just south of town.
The Kaibab National Forest, about 1.6 million acres, is headquartered in Williams.
Grand Canyon Village on the South Rim, the park's main visitor area, is roughly an hour to an hour and a half away.
sports: The Northern Arizona University Lumberjacks compete in NCAA Division I, mostly in the Big Sky Conference, in Flagstaff.
The Arizona Snowbowl ski area is near Flagstaff.
AZ|Williams.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Williams above the US average, with groceries and utilities slightly below it.
AZ|Williams.climate: Williams has a cooler, wetter climate than most of Arizona. Typical daily highs are around 47°F in January and 84°F in July, and August is the wettest month.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Flagstaff.
The main VA medical center for northern Arizona is in Prescott.
around: Flagstaff is roughly 40 minutes east on Interstate 40.
Sedona, known for its sandstone formations and hiking trails, is roughly an hour and a quarter away.
Kingman is roughly two hours west.

AZ|Quartzsite.intro: Quartzsite is a town of about 2,400 people in La Paz County, right on Interstate 10. Winter visitors in RVs are a big part of local life, and major gem and mineral shows are held there, mostly in January and February.
family: The Quartzsite Museum is housed in Tyson's Well Stage Station, built beginning in 1866.
The gem and mineral shows fill the town each January and February.
London Bridge in Lake Havasu City is roughly an hour and a half to two hours away.
outdoors: The Dome Rock Mountains overlook the town on the west.
The Arizona Peace Trail, an off-highway route, passes through Quartzsite.
Kofa National Wildlife Refuge, southeast of town, offers desert wildlife viewing, rock climbing and remote camping.
sports: The Yuma Jaycees Silver Spur Rodeo is held every February in Yuma.
AZ|Quartzsite.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Quartzsite far below the US average, with groceries below average and utilities slightly above.
AZ|Quartzsite.climate: Quartzsite has a hot desert climate, with mild to warm winters from November to March and very hot summers. Typical daily highs run about 67°F in January and about 109°F in July.
vets: The VA lists a clinic in Yuma.
The main VA medical center for southern Arizona is in Tucson.
around: Blythe, California, on the Colorado River, is roughly half an hour away by car.
Parker, the county seat, is roughly 45 minutes away.
Yuma is roughly an hour and a half to two hours away.

AZ|Willcox.intro: Willcox is a city of about 3,200 people in Cochise County, in the Sulphur Springs Valley of southeastern Arizona. Agriculture, wine production and tourism are its main industries, and Interstate 10 runs just north of town.
family: Rex Allen Days, held since 1951 on the first weekend in October, includes a parade, rodeos and a car show.
Willcox West Fest, usually in April, features a rodeo and a chuck wagon cook-off.
A Christmas light parade and craft fair is held in December.
outdoors: Chiricahua National Monument, about 36 miles southeast, has hoodoos, balancing rocks and about 17 miles of trails.
Sandhill cranes winter in the area around the Willcox Playa, a dry lakebed five miles south of town.
Fort Bowie National Historic Site preserves a 19th-century Army outpost, reached by a 1.5-mile foot trail.
food: Willcox is the largest wine grape growing region in Arizona.
Wine country festivals in spring and fall, usually the third weekends of May and October, include live music and arts and crafts.
sports: The University of Arizona Wildcats, in Tucson, compete in the Big 12 Conference.
AZ|Willcox.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Willcox far below the US average, with groceries below average and utilities above.
AZ|Willcox.climate: Willcox has a semi-arid climate, and summer monsoon rains bring it more rainfall than Tucson or Phoenix. Typical daily highs are about 61°F in January and about 96°F in July.
vets: VA clinics are in Safford, roughly an hour away, and Sierra Vista.
The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for the region.
Fort Huachuca, a U.S. Army post, is at Sierra Vista.
around: Benson, about 35 miles west on Interstate 10, is the gateway to Kartchner Caverns State Park.
Tucson, with its international airport and the University of Arizona, is about 80 miles west on Interstate 10.

AZ|Tucson.intro: Tucson is a city of about 540,000 people in southern Arizona. It is the county seat of Pima County and the home of the University of Arizona.
family: Reid Park, the city's largest park, includes the Reid Park Zoo.
The Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, west of town, blends a zoo, an aquarium and a botanical garden on 98 acres.
The Pima Air and Space Museum has close to 400 aircraft on 80 acres of grounds.
outdoors: Saguaro National Park has two districts, about 10 miles west and east of Tucson, with 165 miles of trails.
The Catalina Highway climbs Mount Lemmon from east Tucson, where the summit can be 20 to 30 degrees cooler than the valley.
Rillito River Park has a multi-use path for biking and walking.
food: Tucson was named the first American UNESCO City of Gastronomy in 2015.
Mission Garden, west of downtown at the foot of Sentinel Peak, grows heritage crops and heirloom trees.
sports: The University of Arizona Wildcats compete in NCAA Division I in the Big 12 Conference.
Wildcats baseball has won four national championships, and men's basketball won the national title in 1997.
AZ|Tucson.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and groceries in Tucson a little below the US average, with utilities close to average.
AZ|Tucson.climate: Summers are very hot and winters are mild. At nearby Saguaro National Park, typical daily highs are around 101°F in June and July and in the mid to upper 60s from December through February.
vets: The Tucson VA Medical Center is the main VA location for southern Arizona.
VA clinics are also in Green Valley, Casa Grande and Sierra Vista.
around: Phoenix is about 116 miles away by interstate, roughly two hours by car.
Nogales, on the Mexican border, is roughly an hour and a quarter away.
Sierra Vista is roughly an hour and a half away.

CA|Big Bear.intro: Big Bear is a mountain community in the San Bernardino Mountains. The city of Big Bear Lake, with about 5,000 people, sits on the south shore of the lake it is named for, next to Big Bear City.
family: Big Bear Lake has held an Oktoberfest every year since 1970.
A branch of the San Bernardino County Library serves the community.
The Big Bear Solar Observatory sits on the lake.
outdoors: Big Bear Lake is a large recreational lake with trout, bass and catfish.
San Bernardino National Forest surrounds the area and has many trails of varying difficulty.
The Pacific Crest Trail passes by Big Bear City.
sports: Snow Summit and Bear Mountain are the two ski resorts in the area.
The first Winter X Games were held in Big Bear Lake in 1997.
CA|Big Bear.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Big Bear Lake well above the US average, with groceries close to average and utilities somewhat above.
CA|Big Bear.climate: Winters are cold and bring significant snow, averaging close to 59 inches a season at lake level. Typical daily highs run about 46°F in January and about 80°F in July.
vets: The VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda.
VA clinics are also in Redlands, Rancho Cucamonga and Victorville.
around: San Bernardino is about 25 miles away, roughly an hour or more by mountain highway.
Redlands is roughly an hour away by State Route 38.
Ontario International Airport, the closest major airport, is roughly an hour and a half away.

CA|Merced.intro: Merced is a city of about 86,000 people and the county seat of Merced County in the San Joaquin Valley. It is known as the Gateway to Yosemite and is home to the University of California, Merced.
family: Castle Air Museum in Atwater, about 8 miles away, has more than 80 historical aircraft on 35 acres.
Lake Yosemite has shaded picnic areas with tables, barbecue pits and a small playground.
The County Courthouse Museum is one of the city's historic attractions.
outdoors: Lake Yosemite, about 5 miles east of Merced, allows boating and hosts sailing races on summer evenings.
Merced National Wildlife Refuge has wetlands and grasslands with large wintering flocks of sandhill cranes and geese.
Yosemite National Park is less than two hours away by car.
sports: UC Merced's teams compete in the California Pacific Conference in sports including soccer, water polo and basketball.
CA|Merced.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Merced above the US average, with groceries just below it.
CA|Merced.climate: Summers are hot and dry and winters are mild and damp. Typical daily highs run from about 56°F in January to about 96°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Merced.
The main VA medical center for central California is in Fresno.
around: Modesto is about 40 miles north, roughly an hour by car.
Fresno, 55 miles away, is a little over an hour by car.
Turlock is roughly half an hour north on State Route 99.

CA|Barstow.intro: Barstow is a city of about 25,000 people in the Mojave Desert of San Bernardino County, where Interstates 15 and 40 meet.
family: The Route 66 Mother Road Museum and the Western America Railroad Museum are housed in a 1911 Harvey House hotel and train station.
The Desert Discovery Center houses the Old Woman meteorite, the largest meteorite found in California.
Calico Ghost Town, a restored silver mining town and county regional park, is a few miles from Barstow.
outdoors: Rainbow Basin, 8 miles north of Barstow, draws photographers, hikers and campers.
Coyote Dry Lake, a large dry lakebed, is 15 miles northeast of town.
Lava tubes around Pisgah Crater can be explored.
sports: Barstow Community College fields men's and women's basketball, baseball and softball teams.
The city runs adult basketball and softball leagues, and its sports park has lighted ball fields, soccer fields and volleyball courts.
CA|Barstow.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Barstow well below the US average and groceries a little below, with utilities and transportation above average.
CA|Barstow.climate: Barstow has an arid climate with four seasons, very hot summers and cold winter mornings. Typical daily highs run from about 59°F in January to about 102°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Victorville, and the VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda.
Marine Corps Logistics Base Barstow is in the city, and the Army's National Training Center at Fort Irwin is north of town.
around: Victorville is about 32 miles south, roughly 40 minutes by car.
Los Angeles is roughly two hours away.
Las Vegas is roughly two and a half to three hours away.

CA|Blythe.intro: Blythe is a city of about 18,000 people in eastern Riverside County, in the Palo Verde Valley along the Colorado River. Interstate 10 crosses the city from east to west.
family: The city has six parks and a recreation center.
Palo Verde College, a public community college, is in Blythe.
The city also has two museums.
outdoors: The area is popular with campers and hikers, with three boat ramps onto the Colorado River and seven campgrounds.
The Blythe Intaglios, giant ground figures, are north of town.
sports: The city has an 18-hole public golf course.
CA|Blythe.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Blythe well below the US average, with groceries slightly below and utilities somewhat above.
CA|Blythe.climate: Blythe has a hot desert climate with mild winters and extremely hot summers. Typical highs are about 68°F in January and about 109°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Blythe.
The VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda, with another clinic in Palm Desert.
around: Quartzsite, Arizona, known for its winter gem and mineral shows, is roughly half an hour away.
Parker, Arizona, on the Colorado River, is roughly an hour away.
Indio, in the Coachella Valley, is nearly 100 miles west on Interstate 10, and Phoenix is about 150 miles east.

CA|Fresno.intro: Fresno is a city of roughly 540,000 people in California's San Joaquin Valley. It is the county seat of Fresno County and the largest city in the Central Valley region.
family: The Fresno Chaffee Zoo, in Roeding Park, covers 39 acres and houses over 190 species.
Woodward Park has three children's playgrounds, a lake and a Japanese garden.
Forestiere Underground Gardens are a series of hand-built underground rooms and gardens dating from the early 1900s.
outdoors: Woodward Park sits on the San Joaquin River, with trails that link to the Lewis S. Eaton Trail.
Yosemite National Park is about 60 miles north of Fresno.
Sequoia National Park is about 75 miles southeast, and Kings Canyon National Park is about 60 miles east.
food: Fresno is surrounded by some of the country's most productive farmland.
The Tower District is a neighborhood known for community events, including an annual literary festival.
sports: The Fresno State Bulldogs compete in NCAA Division I and have won national championships in softball and baseball.
The Fresno Grizzlies play Single-A baseball at a downtown ballpark.
Woodward Park has hosted the state high school cross country championships since 1987.
CA|Fresno.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Fresno somewhat above the US average, with groceries about average.
CA|Fresno.climate: Fresno has a semi-arid climate with cool, mild winters and long, hot, dry summers. Typical daily highs run from about 55°F in December and January to about 98°F in July, and winter can bring tule fog.
vets: The main VA medical center for central California is in Fresno.
VA clinics are also in Merced, Oakhurst and Visalia.
Naval Air Station Lemoore is roughly 45 minutes away.
around: Visalia is roughly an hour away by car.
Oakhurst, on Highway 41 toward Yosemite, is roughly an hour away.
Merced is 55 miles away, a little over an hour by car.

CA|Borrego Springs.intro: Borrego Springs is a desert village of roughly 3,000 people in northeastern San Diego County, surrounded by Anza-Borrego Desert State Park. It was the first community in California named an International Dark Sky Community, and the town has no stoplights.
family: More than 130 large metal animal sculptures stand in the desert around town.
Julian, a mountain town under an hour away, has held an Apple Days festival since 1949 and has a pioneer museum.
The San Diego Zoo Safari Park is near Escondido, roughly an hour and a half to two hours away.
outdoors: Anza-Borrego Desert State Park surrounds the town and covers about 650,000 acres.
The park has about 110 miles of hiking trails and 12 wilderness areas.
Spring wildflower blooms are among the park's biggest attractions in wet years.
food: Julian is known for its apple pie, and apples remain a local crop.
sports: The San Diego Padres play Major League Baseball in downtown San Diego, roughly two hours away.
An aerobatic club holds competitions at the Borrego Valley Airport each April and October.
CA|Borrego Springs.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Borrego Springs below the US average, with groceries slightly above and utilities above.
CA|Borrego Springs.climate: Winters are mild, with typical daily highs near 70°F in January. Summers are very hot, with highs near 107°F in July.
vets: The VA medical center for the region is in San Diego.
VA clinics are listed in Escondido, El Centro, Oceanside and Chula Vista.
around: Julian is under an hour away by car.
Palm Springs is just under two hours away.
San Diego and its international airport are roughly two hours away.

CA|Bakersfield.intro: Bakersfield is a city of about 400,000 people and the county seat of Kern County, at the southern end of the San Joaquin Valley. It is the birthplace of the country music style known as the Bakersfield sound.
family: The Kern County Museum has regional artifacts and a hands-on children's discovery museum.
The Buena Vista Museum of Natural History has a collection of marine fossils from the region.
The Kern County Fair each September showcases local agriculture with a rodeo, concerts and a carnival.
outdoors: The Kern River Parkway Trail follows the river for hiking and biking.
Panorama Vista Preserve, a 930-acre wildlife refuge in northeast Bakersfield, has hiking trails and biking paths.
Lake Isabella, a Kern River reservoir 35 miles away, is popular with boaters, water skiers and anglers.
food: Basque cooking is a long-standing part of the city's food history.
The Kern County Basque Festival on Memorial Day weekend features food, music, dance and handball.
sports: The Bakersfield Condors play professional hockey in the American Hockey League.
The Cal State Bakersfield Roadrunners compete in NCAA Division I in the Big West Conference.
CA|Bakersfield.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Bakersfield somewhat above the US average, with groceries about average.
CA|Bakersfield.climate: Bakersfield has a hot, dry climate with nearly rainless summers and mild winters with chilly nights. Typical daily highs are about 59°F in January and 98°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Bakersfield.
The main VA medical center for the region is in Los Angeles.
around: Tehachapi, 35 miles east-southeast, is about an hour away and sits near the Pacific Crest Trail.
Los Angeles is roughly two hours away by car.
State Route 99 runs through the city.

CA|Ridgecrest.intro: Ridgecrest is a city of about 28,000 people in northeastern Kern County, in the Indian Wells Valley along U.S. Route 395. It sits next to Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake, the area's main employer.
family: The Maturango Museum covers the natural and cultural history of the northern Mojave Desert and leads tours to Little Petroglyph Canyon.
The Ridgecrest Petroglyph Festival celebrates the area's rock art and native culture each year.
Cerro Coso Community College has its main campus near Ridgecrest.
outdoors: Red Rock Canyon State Park, close to Ridgecrest, offers hiking and camping.
Big and Little Petroglyph Canyons are part of a National Historic Landmark district with over 20,000 petroglyphs.
Lake Isabella, a Kern River reservoir roughly an hour and a half away, is popular with hikers, boaters and anglers.
CA|Ridgecrest.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Ridgecrest well below the US average, with groceries close to average and utilities above.
CA|Ridgecrest.climate: Summers are hot and extremely dry with cool nights, and the area gets under 5 inches of rain a year. Typical daily highs are about 60°F in December and about 105°F in July.
vets: VA clinics are in Lancaster and Bakersfield.
Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake is next to the city.
around: The Lancaster and Palmdale area is about 82 miles away, roughly an hour and a half to two hours by road.
Bakersfield is about 110 miles away, a bit over two hours.
Lone Pine, near the Alabama Hills in the eastern Sierra, is roughly an hour and a half away.

CA|Twentynine Palms.intro: Twentynine Palms is a city of about 28,000 people in the Mojave Desert of San Bernardino County. It is one of the entry points to Joshua Tree National Park, and the Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center is nearby.
family: Luckie Park has grassy areas and playgrounds and hosts fairs and carnivals.
The local historical society runs a history museum in the city's original schoolhouse.
The Oasis of Murals is a series of 26 outdoor murals around town showing desert life and history.
outdoors: Joshua Tree National Park lies just south of town, with its Oasis of Mara entrance in Twentynine Palms.
The park is popular with rock climbers and was designated a Dark Sky Park in 2017.
CA|Twentynine Palms.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Twentynine Palms well below the US average and groceries a little below, with utilities above average.
CA|Twentynine Palms.climate: Winters are moderately cool, with typical daily highs around 63°F in January. Summers are very hot, with highs around 104°F in July.
vets: The VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda, and there is a VA clinic in Palm Desert.
The Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center is at Twentynine Palms.
around: The community of Joshua Tree is about 20 minutes west by car.
Yucca Valley is about half an hour away.
Palm Springs, the closest passenger airport, is a little over an hour away.

CA|Victorville.intro: Victorville is a city of about 135,000 people in the Victor Valley of San Bernardino County, at the southwestern edge of the Mojave Desert in the High Desert.
family: Old Town Victorville, along historic Route 66, has a Route 66 museum and several large murals.
Silverwood Lake State Recreation Area has picnic areas, swimming beaches, boating and fishing.
Big Bear Lake, roughly an hour and 10 minutes away, has held an Oktoberfest every year since 1970.
outdoors: The Mojave River runs through Victorville.
The San Bernardino National Forest offers many hiking trails of varying difficulty and designated camping sites.
CA|Victorville.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Victorville above the US average, with groceries slightly below it.
CA|Victorville.climate: Victorville has a cool arid climate with four distinct seasons. Typical daily highs are about 58°F in January and about 98°F in July, and winter is the wet season.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Victorville.
The VA medical center for the region is in Loma Linda.
around: San Bernardino is about 36 miles south on Interstate 15 through Cajon Pass, roughly 50 minutes by car.
Barstow is about 32 miles north, roughly 40 minutes away.
Big Bear Lake, in the San Bernardino Mountains, is roughly an hour and 10 minutes away.

CA|Visalia.intro: Visalia is a city of about 141,000 people in the San Joaquin Valley and the county seat of Tulare County. It is known as the Gateway to the Sequoias and is the center of one of the country's most productive farm counties.
family: Mooney Grove Park preserves one of the largest valley oak groves in California.
The historic Fox Theatre hosts music and stage performances.
Kaweah Oaks Preserve, a 322-acre nature preserve, is just outside the city.
outdoors: Sequoia National Park, home of the General Sherman Tree, is entered near the town of Three Rivers, roughly 45 minutes away.
Kings Canyon National Park includes Grant Grove and the General Grant tree.
Lake Kaweah is a reservoir on the Kaweah River below Three Rivers.
sports: The Visalia Rawhide play Single-A baseball in the California League.
College of the Sequoias has its main campus in Visalia.
CA|Visalia.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing and utilities in Visalia somewhat above the US average, with groceries close to average.
CA|Visalia.climate: Summers are hot and dry, and most rain falls from November through April. Typical daily highs range from about 55°F in January to about 94°F in July, and winter often brings dense tule fog.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Visalia.
The main VA medical center for central California is in Fresno.
Naval Air Station Lemoore is west of nearby Hanford.
around: Tulare, 8 miles south, hosts the World Ag Expo each February.
Hanford is 18 miles west.
Fresno, the nearest big city with commercial flights, is roughly an hour away by car.

CO|Greenwood Village.intro: Greenwood Village is a city of about 16,000 people in Arapahoe County, on the south side of the Denver area. It grew up around the Denver Technological Center.
family: The Denver Art Museum and the Denver Museum of Nature and Science are in Denver, about 20 minutes away.
Cheyenne Mountain Zoo is in Colorado Springs, roughly an hour south.
The city is home to an 18,000-seat outdoor amphitheater for concerts.
outdoors: Cherry Creek State Park has an 880-acre reservoir, a sand swim beach and about 35 miles of multi-use trails.
The High Line Canal Trail offers roughly 60 miles of path open all year to hikers, bikers and joggers.
sports: Denver's pro teams include the Broncos, Nuggets, Avalanche, Rockies and Rapids.
The Colorado Buffaloes, an NCAA Division I program, are based in Boulder.
CO|Greenwood Village.cost: BestPlaces index figures put housing in Greenwood Village far above the US average, with groceries slightly above and utilities slightly below.
CO|Greenwood Village.climate: The Denver area has four distinct seasons, with most precipitation from April through August. Typical daily highs run from about 45°F in January to about 90°F in July.
vets: The main VA location for eastern Colorado is in Aurora.
VA clinics are in nearby Englewood and Castle Rock.
around: Denver is roughly 20 minutes away by car.
Castle Rock is roughly half an hour south, and Boulder roughly an hour away.
Colorado Springs is roughly an hour south.

CA|Stanford.intro: Stanford is an unincorporated community of about 21,000 people in northwest Santa Clara County, next to Palo Alto. It is home to Stanford University.
family: The Cantor Center for Visual Arts and the Rodin Sculpture Garden are landmarks on the Stanford campus
The Children's Discovery Museum of San Jose is in nearby San Jose
The Santa Cruz Museum of Natural History is in Santa Cruz
outdoors: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve is a 1,200-acre natural reserve west of the central Stanford campus
Foothills Park and Pearson–Arastradero Preserve are part of the Palo Alto park system
Half Moon Bay has several state beaches on the Pacific coast
sports: Stanford Cardinal teams compete in 36 varsity sports in NCAA Division I and the Atlantic Coast Conference
The San Jose Sharks and San Jose Earthquakes play their home games in San Jose
The San Francisco Giants and Golden State Warriors play their home games in San Francisco
CA|Stanford.cost: Figures here are for neighboring Palo Alto. Housing and grocery costs are well above the national average, and miscellaneous costs are also above it, while utilities are somewhat below it.
CA|Stanford.climate: Stanford has warm, dry summers and cool, wet winters. Average daily highs run about 56 °F in January and about 78 °F in July, and average rainfall is about 15 inches a year.
vets: The VA Palo Alto Health Care System's main locations are in Palo Alto, Livermore, and Menlo Park
It also lists clinics in Capitola, Fremont, Marina, and San Jose
around: San Jose is about 20 miles away, roughly 30 minutes by car
San Francisco is about 37 miles away, roughly 50 minutes by car
Half Moon Bay, Oakland, and Santa Cruz are roughly 35, 55, and 60 minutes by car

CA|Thermal.intro: Thermal is an unincorporated community of about 2,700 people in the Coachella Valley of Riverside County. It sits about 25 miles southeast of Palm Springs and about 9.5 miles north of the Salton Sea.
family: The Riverside County Fair and National Date Festival, held each February in Indio, has celebrated the local date crop since 1947
The Living Desert Zoo and Gardens in Palm Desert combines a zoo with a botanical garden of desert plants and animals
The Children's Discovery Museum of the Desert is in nearby Rancho Mirage
outdoors: Joshua Tree National Park, roughly an hour and a half away, is known for its Joshua trees, rock formations, and dark night skies
The Salton Sea State Recreation Area offers fishing, swimming, and camping on the northeast side of the Salton Sea
The Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains National Monument allows hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, and camping in most areas
food: The Indio International Tamale Festival is held each December on the streets of Old Town Indio
sports: The Coachella Valley Firebirds are a professional ice hockey team in the American Hockey League that plays home games in Thousand Palms
Polo season runs from January to March in Indio
CA|Thermal.cost: Groceries and housing are below the national average in Thermal, while utilities and miscellaneous costs are above it.
CA|Thermal.climate: Summers are very hot, with average daytime highs above 100 °F from June through September, peaking near 107 °F in July. Winters are warm, with average January highs around 71 °F.
vets: The VA Loma Linda health care system has a clinic in Palm Desert
The main VA medical center is in Loma Linda
around: Indio is roughly 10 to 15 minutes away by car
Palm Desert is roughly half an hour away
Palm Springs is roughly 40 minutes away

CO|Holyoke.intro: Holyoke is the county seat of Phillips County on the northeast Colorado plains, with about 2,300 residents.
outdoors: North Sterling State Park, about 11 miles north of Sterling, offers fishing, boating, camping and about 6 miles of trails.
Julesburg sits on the north side of the South Platte River, less than a mile from the Nebraska state line.
sports: Northeastern Junior College in Sterling, whose teams are the Plainsmen, fields baseball, basketball, rodeo and softball teams.
CO|Holyoke.cost: Housing costs are well below the US average, while grocery, utility and miscellaneous costs are close to it.
CO|Holyoke.climate: Holyoke has a dry plains climate with cold winters and warm summers. Typical daily highs run from about 42°F in January to about 88°F in July, with about 30 inches of snow a year.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Sterling.
Other VA clinics in the same system include Fort Collins and Loveland.
around: Sterling is roughly an hour and a quarter away and is home to Northeastern Junior College.
Julesburg, on the old Pony Express route, is under an hour away.
Wray is roughly 45 minutes away, and Denver is roughly three and a half hours.

CO|Lone Tree.intro: Lone Tree is a city of about 15,000 people in northern Douglas County, roughly 18 miles south of downtown Denver.
family: The city-owned Lone Tree Arts Center produces its own professional shows and hosts touring performers.
Schweiger Ranch, a homestead founded in 1874, is open to the public as a living history museum.
The Denver Museum of Nature and Science is in Denver, roughly half an hour away.
outdoors: Bluffs Regional Park is a 235-acre open space in southern Lone Tree with a 2.7-mile loop trail and views of the Front Range.
Chatfield State Park centers on a reservoir and is known for more than 300 bird species.
Roxborough State Park is known for red sandstone formations and has six hiking trails.
sports: Denver's pro teams include the Broncos in the NFL, the Nuggets in the NBA and the Avalanche in the NHL.
The Colorado Rockies and Colorado Rapids also play in the Denver area.
CO|Lone Tree.cost: Housing costs are far above the national average, and miscellaneous costs are well above it. Groceries run a little above the national average, while utilities run slightly below it.
CO|Lone Tree.climate: Winters are chilly and snowy, and summers are warm to hot. In nearby Castle Rock, typical daily highs run from about 46°F in January to about 86°F in July.
vets: The main VA location for eastern Colorado is in Aurora.
A VA clinic is in nearby Castle Rock.
around: Light rail lines run from Lone Tree toward Denver, and Interstate 25 passes through the city.
Colorado Springs, roughly an hour south, has Garden of the Gods park and sits near the foot of Pikes Peak.
Boulder, roughly an hour northwest, is home to the University of Colorado Boulder.

DE|Georgetown.intro: Georgetown is the Sussex County seat in southern Delaware, inland from the Atlantic beaches, with about 7,000 residents. Its historic center, The Circle, holds the town hall and the historic county courthouse.
family: Return Day, held every two years two days after Election Day, is a half-day parade and festival in Georgetown.
Trap Pond State Park's nature center offers hayrides, guided nature walks and pontoon boat tours.
Cape Henlopen State Park has a nature center with marine aquariums and swimming beaches with lifeguards in summer.
outdoors: Trap Pond State Park, near Laurel, covers nearly 4,000 acres and is known for its bald cypress trees and canoeing and kayaking.
Cape Henlopen State Park, next to Lewes, has ocean beaches, a fishing pier, dunes and marked trails.
Redden State Forest, just north of Georgetown, covers over 12,000 acres with hiking, horseback riding and nature watching.
sports: Georgetown Speedway draws race fans during its season.
Dover Motor Speedway hosts a NASCAR race weekend each year.
The Delmarva Shorebirds play minor league baseball in Salisbury, Maryland.
DE|Georgetown.cost: Housing and miscellaneous costs are below the US average, while groceries and utilities are slightly above it.
DE|Georgetown.climate: Summers are warm, with typical July highs near 88°F, and winters are cool, with typical January highs near 45°F.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Georgetown.
The main VA medical center is in Wilmington, with another clinic in Dover.
around: Rehoboth Beach, on the Atlantic Ocean, has a mile-long boardwalk and is roughly half an hour away.
Lewes sits beside Cape Henlopen State Park and is roughly half an hour away.
Dover, the state capital and home of Dover Air Force Base, is roughly an hour away.

DE|Newark.intro: Newark is a city of about 31,000 people in New Castle County and is home to the University of Delaware. It is part of the Philadelphia metropolitan area.
family: The city has 36 parks, with roughly 700 acres of parkland and open space and 21 miles of trails.
Winterthur, north of Wilmington, holds a large collection of American decorative arts and has gardens with a narrated tram ride.
Longwood Gardens in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania, covers more than 1,100 acres of gardens, woodlands and meadows and is open year-round.
outdoors: White Clay Creek State Park covers more than 3,500 acres, with 40 miles of trails for hiking and mountain biking.
Lums Pond State Park surrounds Delaware's largest freshwater pond, with boating, fishing and camping.
The Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area covers 5,613 acres just across the Maryland line.
sports: The University of Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens compete in NCAA Division I with 22 varsity teams.
Baltimore is home to the Orioles in Major League Baseball and the Ravens in the NFL.
Philadelphia, roughly an hour away, has five professional sports teams.
DE|Newark.cost: Grocery, utility and miscellaneous costs in Newark are above the US average, while housing costs are about the same as it.
DE|Newark.climate: Summers are warm and humid with frequent afternoon storms, and winters are moderate to cold with occasional snow. Typical daytime highs are about 43°F in January and 89°F in July.
vets: The main VA medical center for the area is in Wilmington.
A VA clinic is in Dover.
around: Wilmington is roughly half an hour away by car, and Philadelphia roughly an hour.
Newark's rail station is on the Northeast Corridor, and Interstate 95 runs through the city.
Rehoboth Beach, an Atlantic coast town with a mile-long boardwalk, is roughly two hours away.

DE|Wilmington.intro: Wilmington is a city of about 71,000 people and the county seat of New Castle County. It sits where the Christina and Delaware rivers meet.
family: The Delaware Art Museum has studio art classes, a children's learning area and a 9-acre sculpture park.
The Brandywine Zoo, created in 1905, sits inside Brandywine Park.
Brandywine Park has playgrounds, athletic fields, a rose garden and a cherry blossom garden.
outdoors: Brandywine Park, the first city park Wilmington established, has walking trails with views of the creek.
Brandywine Creek State Park, three miles north of the city, has eighteen miles of trails and bass fishing in the creek.
The park's nature center offers guided nature walks, birding programs and hayrides.
food: Little Italy hosts an annual Italian festival in the summer.
The city also has an annual Greek cultural festival.
sports: The Wilmington Blue Rocks play minor league baseball in the city.
Philadelphia is home to the Phillies, Eagles, 76ers and Flyers, and the Philadelphia Union of Major League Soccer.
DE|Wilmington.cost: Housing costs are below the national average, while groceries, utilities and miscellaneous costs are above it. Delaware has no sales tax.
DE|Wilmington.climate: Wilmington has hot, humid summers and cool to cold winters, with precipitation spread evenly through the year. Typical daily highs are about 41°F in January and about 87°F in July.
vets: The main VA medical center is in Wilmington.
VA clinics are in Dover and Georgetown.
around: Philadelphia is about 33 miles away.
Newark, about 8 miles away and home to the University of Delaware, is roughly 25 minutes by car.
Rehoboth Beach, with a mile-long boardwalk on the Atlantic, is about two hours away.

FL|Old Town.intro: Old Town is an unincorporated community in Dixie County, in Florida's Big Bend region. It sits on the west bank of the Suwannee River, where US 19, US 98 and State Road 349 meet.
family: The annual Watermelon Festival in nearby Chiefland dates back to 1954.
Manatee Springs State Park, near Chiefland, has a large spring that flows into the Suwannee River.
outdoors: The 31.7-mile Nature Coast State Trail follows an abandoned rail line and has a trailhead in Old Town.
Manatee Springs State Park is about six miles west of Chiefland.
The Lower Suwannee National Wildlife Refuge offers wildlife watching, fishing, canoeing and hunting.
sports: The Florida Gators, the University of Florida's teams, compete in the Southeastern Conference and play on campus in Gainesville.
FL|Old Town.climate: Old Town has a humid subtropical climate with a rainy season from June through September. In nearby Cross City, typical daily highs run about 66°F in January and about 91°F in July.
vets: The VA has medical centers in Gainesville and Lake City.
around: Cross City, the county seat, is roughly 15 minutes away by car.
Chiefland is roughly 15 minutes away.
Gainesville, home to the University of Florida, is a little over an hour away.

FL|Panacea.intro: Panacea is a small fishing community of about 700 people in Wakulla County, on the Gulf coast south of Tallahassee.
family: The Gulf Specimen Marine Laboratory, a not-for-profit research and education group, runs a public aquarium in Panacea.
Its touch tanks let visitors handle marine creatures, and it offers guided marsh walks.
outdoors: Ochlockonee River State Park, where the river meets Ochlockonee Bay, offers camping, canoeing, kayaking, fishing and hiking trails.
Edward Ball Wakulla Springs State Park, south of Tallahassee, is built around a very large freshwater spring and offers boat tours.
St. Marks National Wildlife Refuge covers more than 83,000 acres, includes the St. Marks Lighthouse, and is crossed by the Florida National Scenic Trail.
food: Panacea and nearby Ochlockonee Bay support small fishing fleets.
Apalachicola hosts the Florida Seafood Festival every year.
sports: The Florida State Seminoles play college football in Tallahassee.
FL|Panacea.cost: Housing and miscellaneous costs in Panacea are below the national average, while grocery and utility costs are above it.
FL|Panacea.climate: Summers are long, hot and humid with brief afternoon thunderstorms, and winters are short and mild. In Tallahassee, typical daily highs run about 64°F in January and about 92°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Tallahassee.
VA medical centers are in Gainesville and Lake City.
around: Crawfordville, the county seat, is roughly 20 minutes away.
Tallahassee, the state capital, is roughly 50 minutes away.
Carrabelle is roughly 40 minutes away, and Apalachicola roughly an hour and a quarter.

FL|Defuniak Springs.intro: DeFuniak Springs is a city of about 6,000 people in the Florida Panhandle and the county seat of Walton County.
family: The historic district includes the 260-acre Chipley Park and Lake DeFuniak.
The Walton County Heritage Museum is housed in the former railroad depot.
The Walton-DeFuniak Library is a long-standing landmark on the lake.
outdoors: Lake DeFuniak is a spring-fed lake that is nearly perfectly round.
Ponce de Leon Springs State Park lets visitors swim in its spring and hike its nature trails.
Grayton Beach State Park, between Panama City Beach and Destin, has white sand beaches, dunes and places to swim, fish and hike.
food: The Destin Seafood Festival is held one weekend every October.
Pensacola also holds an annual seafood festival downtown.
sports: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos play minor league baseball.
The Pensacola Ice Flyers play minor league hockey.
The University of West Florida Argonauts compete in NCAA Division II.
FL|Defuniak Springs.cost: Housing and groceries are below the US average, utilities are above it, and miscellaneous costs are close to it.
FL|Defuniak Springs.climate: DeFuniak Springs has a humid subtropical climate with plenty of rain, especially in summer, and some exposure to tropical storms. Typical highs are about 62°F in January and about 92°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic at Eglin Air Force Base.
Other VA clinics are in Panama City Beach and Pensacola.
around: Crestview is 29 miles west on US 90, roughly 45 minutes away.
Destin, known for its white beaches and emerald green water, is roughly an hour away.
Pensacola is about 80 miles west on Interstate 10.

FL|Pensacola.intro: Pensacola is a city of about 54,000 people in the Florida Panhandle and the county seat of Escambia County. It is a seaport on Pensacola Bay, sheltered by the barrier island of Santa Rosa.
family: The National Naval Aviation Museum, on Naval Air Station Pensacola, has more than 150 aircraft and spacecraft on display.
The Blue Angels, the Navy's flight demonstration squadron, are based at the air station and hold practice demonstrations there for much of the year.
The Pensacola Lighthouse and Museum is also on the air station.
outdoors: Gulf Islands National Seashore includes beaches, historic forts and mainland areas near Pensacola.
Fort Pickens, completed in 1834, is open to the public within the seashore and is one endpoint of the Florida Trail.
The Pensacola Beach Gulf Pier is used for fishing and wildlife watching.
food: Pensacola holds an annual seafood festival downtown.
sports: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos play minor league baseball.
The Pensacola Ice Flyers play minor league hockey.
The University of West Florida Argonauts compete in NCAA Division II.
FL|Pensacola.cost: Housing costs are well below the US average, while utilities run somewhat above it. Grocery and miscellaneous costs are slightly below average.
FL|Pensacola.climate: Pensacola has short, mild winters and hot, humid summers, with typical daily highs of about 63°F in January and about 92°F in July. Its Gulf Coast location leaves it exposed to hurricanes.
vets: The VA has two locations in Pensacola.
Naval Air Station Pensacola is an active Navy base in the area.
around: Mobile, Alabama, known for its Mardi Gras celebration, is about 59 miles to the west.
Destin, known for its white beaches and emerald green water, is about 48 miles east on US 98.
Milton, the Santa Rosa County seat, is home to the West Florida Railroad Museum and a state rail trail.

GA|Atlanta.intro: Atlanta is the capital of Georgia and the county seat of Fulton County, with about 500,000 residents in the city itself.
family: Zoo Atlanta, in Grant Park, has more than 1,000 animals of over 220 species.
The High Museum of Art is the city's main art museum.
The Michael C. Carlos Museum at Emory University holds a large collection of ancient art.
outdoors: The Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area protects a 48-mile stretch of river between Atlanta and Lake Lanier, with trails and trout fishing.
Stone Mountain Park, about 15 miles east of Atlanta, has a summit trail and an aerial tram.
The BeltLine is a multi-use trail that follows a former 22-mile freight rail loop around the central city.
sports: The Atlanta Braves play Major League Baseball, and the Atlanta Falcons play in the NFL.
Atlanta United FC plays in Major League Soccer.
The Atlanta Hawks play in the NBA and the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA.
GA|Atlanta.cost: Housing costs in Atlanta are above the US average, while grocery costs are close to it. Utilities and miscellaneous costs are a little above average.
GA|Atlanta.climate: Atlanta has hot, humid summers and mild but variable winters. Typical highs are around 90°F in July and around 54°F in January, and snow is light and rare.
vets: The main VA medical center is in Decatur.
VA clinics are in Marietta, Covington, Lawrenceville and other nearby cities.
around: Marietta, about 21 miles northwest, has a historic town square and an art museum.
Athens, about 70 miles northeast, is home to the University of Georgia and the Georgia Museum of Art.
Macon, about 85 miles southeast, has Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park.

GA|Hinesville.intro: Hinesville is a city of about 35,000 people and the county seat of Liberty County. It lies on the south side of Fort Stewart, about 39 miles from Savannah.
family: Georgia Southern University has a Liberty campus in Hinesville.
Richmond Hill hosts community events at its main park, including a Fourth of July festival with fireworks.
Mill Creek Regional Park in Statesboro has athletic fields and a water park.
outdoors: Fort McAllister State Park covers 1,725 acres on the Ogeechee River near Richmond Hill, with a salt marsh and an earthwork fort.
Tybee Island is a barrier island with a sandy beach, about 18 miles east of Savannah.
The Tybee Island Light Station, first built in 1736, is a historic lighthouse on the island.
sports: The Georgia Southern Eagles are the teams of Georgia Southern University in Statesboro, roughly an hour and a half away.
GA|Hinesville.cost: Housing costs are well below the national average, and grocery and miscellaneous costs are somewhat below it. Utilities run slightly above the national average.
GA|Hinesville.climate: Summers are hot and winters are mild. At Fort Stewart next door, typical highs are near 92°F in July and near 63°F in January.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Hinesville.
Other VA clinics are in Savannah and Brunswick.
Fort Stewart, an Army post, borders the city.
around: Savannah, about 39 miles northeast and roughly 55 minutes away, has a historic district with 22 parklike squares.
Richmond Hill, roughly 35 minutes away, lies along Interstate 95.
Brunswick, about 55 miles south, sits beside the barrier islands of Jekyll and St. Simons.

IA|Fort Dodge.intro: Fort Dodge is the county seat of Webster County in north central Iowa, along the Des Moines River, with about 25,000 residents.
family: The Fort Museum and Frontier Village on the southwest edge of town recreates a 19th-century military outpost and village.
Oleson Park has woods, hiking trails and a restored band shell.
The Blanden Memorial Art Museum, opened in 1932, offers art classes for children and adults.
outdoors: Dolliver Memorial State Park, 10 miles south of Fort Dodge, has high bluffs on the Des Moines River, a campground and a boat ramp.
John F. Kennedy Park has a large campground, a lake with a swimming beach and hiking trails.
The 300-acre Gypsum City Off-Highway Vehicle Park was built on former gypsum mines.
sports: The Iowa Central Tritons, of Iowa Central Community College in Fort Dodge, compete in sports including football, wrestling and track and field.
The Iowa State Cyclones play in Ames.
IA|Fort Dodge.cost: Fort Dodge is below the US average for groceries, utilities and miscellaneous costs, and well below it for housing.
IA|Fort Dodge.climate: Fort Dodge has cold winters and hot, humid summers. Typical daily highs run from about 26°F in January to about 83°F in July.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Fort Dodge.
The main VA location for central Iowa is in Des Moines.
around: Webster City, roughly half an hour away, has a 5.7-mile recreational trail along the Boone River.
Ames, home to Iowa State University, is about an hour to an hour and a half away.
Des Moines, the state capital, is about an hour and a half to two hours away.

IA|Davenport.intro: Davenport is the county seat of Scott County in eastern Iowa, on the Mississippi River, and one of the Quad Cities. It has roughly 100,000 residents.
family: The Figge Art Museum, on the north bank of the Mississippi River, holds more than 4,000 works from the 16th century to the present.
The Putnam Museum and Science Center combines regional history and natural science with an interactive science center.
Annual festivals in Davenport include the Mississippi Valley Fair and the Bix Beiderbecke Memorial Jazz Festival.
outdoors: Davenport has more than 50 parks and over 20 miles of recreational paths for biking and walking.
Vander Veer Botanical Park is a 33-acre botanical garden with a conservatory, a rose garden and a fountain.
sports: The Quad Cities River Bandits play minor league baseball in Davenport.
The University of Iowa Hawkeyes play in Iowa City.
IA|Davenport.cost: Housing costs in Davenport are well below the national average. Grocery and utility costs are somewhat below it, and miscellaneous costs are somewhat above it.
IA|Davenport.climate: Summers are warm to hot and humid, with typical July highs around 84°F. Winters are cold and often windy, with January highs around 30°F and snow likely from November through February.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Davenport.
The VA medical center is in Iowa City.
around: Moline, Illinois, another of the Quad Cities, is roughly 20 minutes away by car.
Iowa City, home of the University of Iowa, is about 60 miles west, a little over an hour by car.
Cedar Rapids is roughly an hour and a half away.

IA|Clinton.intro: Clinton is the county seat of Clinton County in eastern Iowa, on the Mississippi River, with about 24,000 residents.
family: Riverview Park has a large municipal swimming pool, a skate park, a playground and public boat ramps.
The Clinton Area Showboat Theatre is a summer professional theatre in a former towboat docked on the levee.
The Sawmill Museum teaches about the lumber industry and the history of Clinton.
outdoors: Eagle Point Park covers 164 acres on bluffs above the Mississippi River, with about 3 miles of hiking trails and a restored prairie.
The Upper Mississippi River National Wildlife and Fish Refuge passes through Clinton along the river.
The Mississippi River Trail passes through Clinton, and the city has many walking and biking trails.
sports: The Clinton LumberKings are a summer collegiate baseball team that plays home games on the riverfront.
IA|Clinton.cost: Housing costs are far below the US average, while groceries are slightly below it and utilities and miscellaneous costs are close to it.
IA|Clinton.climate: Winters are cold and snowy, with typical January highs near 29°F. Summers are warm, with typical July highs near 84°F.
vets: The VA has clinics in Davenport, Dubuque and Cedar Rapids.
The VA medical center is in Iowa City.
around: Davenport, under an hour away, has the Figge Art Museum and the annual Bix Beiderbecke Memorial Jazz Festival.
Dubuque, about an hour to an hour and a half away, has the Fenelon Place Elevator and the National Mississippi River Museum and Aquarium.
Maquoketa, under an hour away, is near Maquoketa Caves State Park.

GA|Newnan.intro: Newnan is the county seat of Coweta County, about 40 miles southwest of Atlanta, with about 43,000 residents. Its motto is "City of Homes."
family: The Coweta County African American Heritage Museum and Research Center focuses on African-American history and local family records.
Callaway Gardens near Pine Mountain, about an hour's drive away, has a butterfly center and a birds of prey show.
The Little White House in Warm Springs, President Franklin D. Roosevelt's retreat, is a state historic site open to visitors.
outdoors: Chattahoochee Bend State Park in Coweta County covers 2,910 acres along the Chattahoochee River, with about 12 miles of hiking trails.
F.D. Roosevelt State Park near Pine Mountain covers 9,049 acres and includes the 23-mile Pine Mountain Trail.
The Carrollton Greenbelt is an 18-mile paved loop for walking and bicycling around Carrollton.
sports: Atlanta is home to the Braves, Falcons, Hawks, Dream and Atlanta United FC.
College teams include the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets and Georgia State Panthers in Atlanta and the West Georgia Wolves in Carrollton.
The annual Peachtree Road Race, a 10 km race, is held in Atlanta.
GA|Newnan.cost: Grocery and housing costs are below the US average, while utilities and miscellaneous costs are slightly above it.
GA|Newnan.climate: Newnan has a moderate climate, with typical January highs around 52°F and typical July highs around 89°F. Rain is spread across the year, and snow is rare.
vets: The VA has a clinic in Newnan.
The main VA medical center is in Decatur, and another clinic is in Carrollton.
around: Downtown Atlanta is about 40 miles northeast on Interstate 85, roughly an hour's drive.
Carrollton, about 22 miles northwest, is home to the University of West Georgia.
Peachtree City has over 100 miles of golf cart paths.

GA|Kennesaw.intro: Kennesaw is a suburban city of about 33,000 people in Cobb County, northwest of Atlanta, and is home to Kennesaw State University.
family: The Southern Museum of Civil War and Locomotive History houses The General, the locomotive from the 1862 Great Locomotive Chase.
The annual Big Shanty Festival, held every April, begins with a parade through downtown.
outdoors: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park is a Civil War battlefield with 17.3 miles of interpretive hiking trails.
Lake Allatoona is a reservoir with marinas, public boat ramps and campgrounds, and Red Top Mountain State Park sits on its shores.
sports: The Kennesaw State Owls compete in 17 varsity sports.
The Atlanta area is home to the Braves, Hawks, Falcons, Dream and Atlanta United FC.
GA|Kennesaw.cost: Housing is the category furthest above the US average, with utilities and miscellaneous costs also above it. Grocery costs are slightly below the US average.
GA|Kennesaw.climate: Kennesaw has hot, humid summers and mild winters. Typical daily highs are about 52°F in January and about 89°F in July.
vets: The VA has clinics in Marietta.
The main VA medical center is in Decatur.
around: Marietta, the Cobb County seat, is 7 miles southeast, roughly 15 minutes by car, and has a historic downtown square.
Downtown Atlanta is 27 miles southeast on Interstate 75.
Acworth, 6 miles northwest, sits on Lake Acworth and Lake Allatoona.

IA|Des Moines.intro: Des Moines is the capital of Iowa and the county seat of Polk County, with about 214,000 residents.
family: Blank Park Zoo is a 49-acre zoo on the south side of Des Moines.
The Science Center of Iowa includes a dome theater.
The Greater Des Moines Botanical Garden is a large botanical garden and greenhouse on the east side of the river.
outdoors: Saylorville Lake is a reservoir on the Des Moines River a few miles upstream from the city.
Boating, swimming, camping and fishing are popular at the lake, and Jester Park and Big Creek State Park are around it.
Ada Hayden Heritage Park in Ames has a lake, wetlands and trails.
food: The Iowa State Fair, held every August, is known for its food on a stick.
The World Food Prize Foundation is based in Des Moines.
sports: The Iowa Cubs play minor league baseball in Des Moines.
The Iowa State Cyclones play football in Ames.
IA|Des Moines.cost: Housing costs in Des Moines are well below the national average, and grocery and utility costs are a little below it. Miscellaneous costs are above the national average.
IA|Des Moines.climate: Des Moines has warm to hot, humid summers and cold, dry winters. Typical daytime highs are about 31°F in January and about 86°F in July.
vets: The main VA location for central Iowa is in Des Moines.
VA clinics are also in Carroll, Fort Dodge, Knoxville and Mason City.
around: Ames, about 30 miles north and under an hour away, is home to Iowa State University.
Ankeny, a suburb in Polk County, is about 20 minutes north.

IA|Sioux City.intro: Sioux City is the county seat of Woodbury County in northwest Iowa, on the Missouri River where Iowa, Nebraska and South Dakota meet. It has about 87,000 residents.
family: The riverfront park includes a dance pavilion and the Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center.
The Sioux City Public Museum downtown has Native American, pioneer, early Sioux City and natural history exhibits.
Saturday in the Park is a music festival held each year near the Fourth of July in Grandview Park.
outdoors: Stone State Park, on the northwestern edge of the city, has many miles of hiking and equestrian trails.
The Dorothy Pecaut Nature Center, within the park, has a butterfly garden and trails where wild turkeys and deer are often seen.
The Sergeant Floyd Monument overlooks the Missouri River valley from a river bluff.
sports: The Sioux City Explorers play baseball in the city.
The Sioux City Musketeers, a hockey team, have played in the city since 1972.
IA|Sioux City.cost: Housing costs are well below the national average, while groceries, utilities and miscellaneous costs are a little below it.
IA|Sioux City.climate: Sioux City has very warm, humid summers and cold, dry winters, with wide temperature swings. Typical highs run about 30°F in January and about 85°F in July.
vets: The main VA location for the area is in Sioux Falls, South Dakota.
The same VA system has a clinic in Spirit Lake, Iowa.
around: Le Mars, under an hour away, holds an annual Ice Cream Days celebration in June.
Yankton, South Dakota, about an hour away, has Lewis and Clark Lake, with camping, swimming and trails.
Sioux Falls, about an hour and a quarter to an hour and a half away, has the Great Plains Zoo.

IL|Granite City.intro: Granite City is a city of about 27,500 people in Madison County, on the Mississippi River in the Metro East part of the St. Louis area.
family: Wilson Park has a pool, an ice rink, a skate park and baseball fields around a paved trail.
The St. Louis Zoo and the Missouri History Museum are both in Forest Park in St. Louis.
The Edwardsville Children's Museum is in nearby Edwardsville.
outdoors: Horseshoe Lake State Park wraps around 2,400-acre Horseshoe Lake, with picnicking, cycling, fishing and small boating.
Madison County has a network of bikeways throughout the county.
Pere Marquette State Park, a few miles north of Alton, has trails for hikers and horseback riders.
food: Collinsville holds a Horseradish Festival each June on its Main Street.
Collinsville's Italian Fest has been held each fall since 1983.
sports: The St. Louis Cardinals play baseball in St. Louis.
The St. Louis Blues play hockey there.
St. Louis City SC plays soccer there.
IL|Granite City.cost: Housing costs in Granite City are far below the national average, and grocery and utility costs are a little below it. Miscellaneous costs run above it.
IL|Granite City.climate: Summers are warm and winters are cold. In nearby Alton, typical daytime highs are near 40°F in January and around 87°F in July.
